title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is part of Grothendieck's case analysis of a system of matrix equations, numbered (33)-(35) in his notes, belonging to his 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The unknowns are ξ, η in SL(M), with M free of rank 2 over a base, and a scalar μ. The data are two fixed matrices ρ and σ. The system includes det ξ = det η = 1, a trace condition on each matrix (Tr ξρ = Tr ρ and Tr ησ = Tr σ, judging from p. 437/438), and the relation ξ = η ε_1(μ−1). Here ε_1(λ) = 1 + λN_1 = (1+N_1)^λ is a one-parameter unipotent subgroup with N_1² = 0.

On the previous page he derived (47), P(ξ) = −Tr ξ(−N_1σ), and (49), N_1 = −(λ_0ρσ^{-1} + 1).

This page.
- From (49), N_1σ = −(λ_0ρ + σ), hence (50): P(ξ) = Tr ξ(λ_0ρ + σ).
- Corollary of the Proposition: the scheme of simultaneous solutions (ξ, η, μ) is relatively smooth of relative dimension 2.
- Reason given: the equation Tr(ξρ) = const cuts out a smooth hypersurface in SL(M) (ρ nowhere vanishing on fibres). On the open set where P(ξ) is invertible, μ = 1/P(ξ) and η = ξ ε_1(μ−1)^{-1} are then determined.

Special case of interest. ρ = [[0,1],[−1,1]] (trace 1, det 1, order 6) and σ = [[0,−1],[1,0]] (order 4). These are the standard generators of SL_2(Z), hence of PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3; this is the modular / genus-1 context.
- I check λ_0 = 1. Then ρσ^{-1} = [[−1,0],[−1,−1]], so N_1 = [[0,0],[1,0]].
- ρ + σ = [[0,0],[0,1]], so P(ξ) = D, the (2,2) entry of ξ. Likewise P'(η) = U.
- (51): η ε_1(μ−1) = [[R+(μ−1)S, S], [T+(μ−1)U, U]] is verified.
- Next page: ε_0(λ) = ρ^{-1}ε_1(λ)ρ = [[1,−λ],[0,1]] is verified.
- The solution scheme is then identified with the affine (Borel-type) group of matrices [[μ, M], [0, 1]], which normalizes ε_0.

The page serves an explicit parametrization of the solution scheme of the 'loop equation' in the SL_2 / modular-group case.
errors: 'sous-schéma lisse de dim 1 de SG(M)': a single equation Tr(ξρ) = c in the 3-dimensional SL_2 gives a surface, i.e. codimension 1 (relative dimension 2). This is consistent with the claimed relative dimension 2 of the solution scheme, so 'dim 1' should read 'codim 1' (a slip or a mis-transcription).

The level set Tr(ξρ) = c is not always smooth when ρ is merely nonvanishing on fibres. The differential vanishes exactly where ρξ is scalar s, i.e. ξ = sρ^{-1} with 2s = c and s² = det ρ. For c = Tr ρ this happens when (Tr ρ)² = 4 det ρ. For ρ = [[0,1],[−1,1]] that means 1 = 4, i.e. in characteristic 3, with singular point ξ = −ρ^{-1}.

That singular point has D = 0, so it is removed by the open condition 'P(ξ) inversible'. The corollary is therefore correct over Z on that open set, but the stated justification needs the open condition or a discriminant hypothesis on ρ.

Next page, (54): from ρ and σ, Tr(ξρ) = C + D − B and Tr(ησ) = S − T. The transcribed 'A+D−B = 1' and 'T−S = 1' do not match. These are either slips in Grothendieck's text or transcription errors; the correct conditions are C + D − B = 1 and S − T = 0.

ideas.what: Smoothness and relative dimension of the scheme of solutions of a system of matrix equations in SL_2 over a general base, via a trace-hypersurface plus an open condition
ideas.modern_name: smoothness of representation/character-type varieties; level sets of trace functions on SL_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (character varieties: Culler-Shalen, Fricke-Klein trace coordinates)

ideas.what: Explicit specialization to the SL_2(Z) generators of order 6 and 4 (Z/2*Z/3 presentation), with the solution scheme identified with an affine group [[μ,M],[0,1]] normalizing a unipotent one-parameter subgroup
ideas.modern_name: explicit solution of loop/braid relations in SL_2; affine group Aff_1 as solution scheme

deep.surprise_reason: Routine explicit matrix computation inside a long case analysis. The algebra checks out (λ_0 = 1, N_1 = [[0,0],[1,0]], P(ξ) = D). The only subtlety is that the char-3 singular point is removed by the open condition, which Grothendieck does not remark on. Nothing here appears new to specialists by itself.
transcription_corrections: 'sur l'équation Tr(ξρ) = cte' should read 'car l'équation Tr(ξρ) = cte'.
'dans il faut prendre ouvert l'ouvert' should read roughly 'dont il faut prendre l'ouvert défini par P(ξ) inversible'.
In (51) the left side is 'η ε_1(μ−1)', not 'ξ_1(μ−1)'.
Previous page: 'N_1 une matrice de carré unité N_1² = 1' must be 'de carré nul, N_1² = 0'. This is required by 1 + λN_1 = (1+N_1)^λ and by N_1 = [[0,0],[1,0]].
'à 1 paramètre' and 'schéma relatif lisse, de dim relative 2' are read correctly. The '{+des équ.+}' insertion is 'des équ.' above 'simultanées'.
